title: Janus Engine — Howl's Moving Castle simulation run 001
purpose: First numerical attempt to start the Janus Engine as a self-driving system and determine whether a positive power margin is mathematically possible after paying internal loads. This is a screening model, not experimental validation.
model_scope: Steady-state lumped 0-D mass/energy balance. The gaseous-O2 branch is treated as the primary start mode; an optional cryogenic/LOX penalty is evaluated separately.

assumptions.assumption_warning: All specific processing energies are provisional placeholders chosen to expose the balance structure. They are not measured Janus values and must be replaced by R0/R0B/R0C/R0D/R0E data.

baseline_gaseous_O2_result.interpretation: Under the assumed low hydraulic pressure drop and placeholder processing costs, the simulated gaseous-O2 system pays its internal loads and leaves approximately 0.74 kW electrical output. This is not yet evidence that the real device can achieve these assumptions.

optional_LOX_branch_result.interpretation: The provisional LOX branch consumes most of the surplus. Therefore first self-drive should use gaseous O2 and keep oxygen liquefaction disabled until measured cryogenic performance is available.

break_even_pressure_drop.design_lesson: Hydrodynamic resistance is a first-order feasibility variable. The rotating gill and water path should target pressure drop far below the theoretical break-even value; approximately 1-2 kPa is used only as an early design target, not a validated limit.

green: There exists a plausible mathematical region with P_net > 0 if dissolved-O2 extraction is substantial and the water-side pressure drop is very low.
Process integration materially helps because N2 and thermal duties are charged as service loads rather than treated as independent throwaway subsystems.
Gaseous-O2 self-drive has a much wider modeled margin than immediate LOX production.
red_or_unknown: No measured rotating-gill extraction fraction yet.
No measured pressure drop for the Axle-derived geometry yet.
No measured energy cost for O2/N2 purification, moisture removal, sorbent regeneration or compression yet.
No selected central engine/fuel or measured shaft efficiency yet.
No demonstrated oxygen-compatible integrated hardware yet.
dominant_killer_variables: specific gas-processing energy per kg O2
fixed mechanical/control losses at small scale

next_action: Freeze a single ring geometry and replace the two most sensitive assumptions first: measure DeltaP_water(Q,RPM) and m_dot_O2(Q,RPM). Re-run this exact balance with measured values before adding LOX or combustion complexity.
safety_boundary: The simulation does not authorize oxygen-enriched combustion, high-pressure oxygen, or cryogenic prototype work. Early physical validation remains low-energy water-loop and gas-transfer measurement with physically separated oxygen-compatible paths.
